name: Velarok
summary: Among the ash and slain dwarves in Searing Gorge, Velarok Windblade asks travelers to help him forge vengeance.

sections.title: A Son's Vengeance
sections.body: Southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade camps in the wastes of Searing Gorge. Dark Iron dwarves lie dead around him, slain in the fight he says began with his father's murder. He asks travelers to gather what he needs to make the Torch of Retribution. The enchanted weapon is meant for the Dark Irons and Ragnaros's minions.

sections.title: The Deceiver Unmasked
sections.body: Velarok's slain father is a lie. Once the Torch of Retribution is assembled and energized, his human guise breaks. Beneath it stands Velarok the Deceiver, a cunning drake of the black dragonflight. He used mortals to weaken the Dark Iron dwarves for his brood's designs. Amused by the help they have given, Velarok spares them. His servant leaves them petty trinkets, and the drake flies toward Blackrock Mountain.

faq.answer: Southeast of Thorium Point in Searing Gorge, Velarok Windblade appears to be a vengeful human swordsman. He seeks retribution against the Dark Iron clan for his father's death.

faq.q: Why is Velarok surrounded by dead dwarves?
faq.answer: Velarok says the Dark Iron dwarves around his camp were killed in the blood feud over his father's death.

faq.q: What is the Torch of Retribution?
aliases: what is the torch of retribution
faq.answer: The Torch of Retribution is an enchanted weapon made from rare materials gathered across Searing Gorge for vengeance. Velarok has his helpers collect the pieces, then combines and enchants them himself before binding the finished torch to the one who helped him.

faq.q: Why does Velarok disguise himself as a human?
faq.answer: A human guise lets Velarok recruit Alliance and Horde adventurers without raising suspicion. Black dragons often take mortal forms to direct attacks against enemies such as Ragnaros's Dark Iron servants.

faq.q: Where does Velarok go after revealing himself?
faq.answer: After revealing his dragon form as Velarok the Deceiver, he flies toward Blackrock Mountain to rejoin his brood. His mortal servant gives trinkets to the adventurers who helped him.

faq.q: Does Velarok attack when his disguise drops?
faq.answer: No. Velarok finds the adventurers' unwitting service amusing and satisfactory. He spares them, and his servant gives them minor trinkets.

angles.text: As a human, Velarok's tale of a murdered father and a son's vengeance appeals to ideals of filial duty and righteous retribution.

As a dwarf, the Dark Iron dwarves are enemies of Ironforge, so a stranger's vow of vengeance against them may find sympathy among Bronzebeards. Yet Searing Gorge holds cunning dangers beyond the Dark Irons.
